players.note: Chase Brown is the RB20 in fantasy points per game just based on volume alone. He has one touchdown all season, and he has averaged 18.5 touches and 75.6 total yards. Brown's role has remained consistent with 75.5% and 68.9% snap rates over the last two games. Overall, he has a 71.4% snap rate with 61.4% of the rushing work, a 57.8% route share, and a 15% target share. Brown has posted a solid 2.21 yards after contact per attempt while also having a disappointing 13% missed tackle rate and 8% explosive run rate. His offensive line hasn't done him many favors with only 1.40 yards before contact per attempt. This week's matchup could finally lead to Brown's first 100-yard day on the ground, though. The Falcons' run defense has fallen off a cliff. In their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Jonathan Taylor has seen his workload scaled back with a 66.4% snap rate, 44.1% of the rushing work, and a 54.7% route share (15.4% target share). In those games, Taylor has averaged 16 touches and 78.5 total yards. Overall, Taylor has a strong 13.7% explosive run rate and 16% missed tackle rate. Even in a reduced capacity, Taylor should have a nice day against Dallas. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the second-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Rhamondre Stevenson remains New England's workhorse back. Stevenson is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14.9 touches and 72.4 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 26th in yards after contact per attempt and seventh in missed tackle rate. Stevenson is a volume-based RB2 again this week. Across their last five games, Green Bay has ranked 15th in rushing success rate while allowing the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

In Week 7, Jonah Coleman led the backfield in snaps (50%), rushing attempts (nine, 34.6%), and was second in route share (21.9%), running one less route than RJ Harvey. Coleman finished with 11 touches and 69 total yards. Last week, his role grew further with RJ Harvey out. Coleman finished with 15 touches and 104 total yards (RB12 for the week) with a 67.9% snap rate, a 47.8% rushing share, and a 50% route share (12.5% target share). This season, among 58 qualifying rushers, Coleman is first in explosive run rate and 19th in missed tackle rate. Coleman is a wonderful fantasy option this week, and he could continue to crush. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.6 touches and 90 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Gordon is eighth in explosive run rate and 23rd in yards after contact per attempt. The only drawback to Gordon has been the lack of passing game involvement. Over his last four games, he has only six targets and zero receiving yards. He has to get it done on early downs, which he has been doing. Gordon will find more uphill sledding this week, though. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. He'll need a touchdown to pay off for fantasy this week, along with all the volume he can handle.

Since Week 6, as the starting back for Houston, Woody Marks has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.5 touches and 74.3 total yards. With that type of volume, the biggest culprit for underperforming in fantasy is the fact that he didn't have a touchdown in either game. In those two games, he played 83.2% of the snaps with 68% of the rushing work and a 56.9% route share (6.5% target share). Among 42 qualifying backs, he is 21st in explosive run rate and 18th in missed tackle rate. Marks is a volume-based RB2 with a good matchup this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Quinshon Judkins had a season-low 39.1% snap rate with 73.3% of the rushing work and only an 18% route share (4.9% target share). In the first seven weeks of the season, Judkins had a 59.2% snap rate and a 30.3% route share. We'll see if this role reduction holds this week, but it's a worry for Judkins moving forward. Judkins is the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.4 touches and 68 total yards. Among 45 qualifying backs, he is 37th in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 32nd in missed tackle rate. If the Browns play with a lead this week, they could load up Judkins with rushing volume. If that happens, he'll have a nice stat line. The Saints have been unable to stop the run. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-highest missed tackle rate.

Derrick Henry might be the RB13 in fantasy points per game overall, but that doesn't tell the entire story. Since Week 4, without Lamar Jackson, he has been the RB28 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.8 touches and 73.6 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, he is still performing well, ranking 18th in explosive run rate and 17th in yards after contact per attempt. Henry is now a volume-based RB2 with a horrible matchup this week. Yes, Jacksonville just lost DaVon Hamilton, but they should still field a solid, if not strong, run defense. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the lowest rushing success rate, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty was turned into the passing-down-only back with a 36.7% snap rate, only two rushing attempts, a 48.1% route share, and an 11.5% target share. I don't know if this is the beginning of a new role for him or punishment for mouthing off to the media about the Jets' run defense. We'll have to wait and see what his usage looks like in Week 9. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty had a 69.5% snap rate, 60.9% of the rushing work, and a 54.8% route share (16.5% target share). Last week, Jeanty finished with five touches and 73 total yards. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty averaged 20 touches and 91.5 total yards (RB14 in fantasy points per game). This season, Jeanty has 2.13 yards after contact per attempt, which is solid, but he has also logged a 12% missed tackle rate and 5.1% explosive run rate. Those last two stats won't get it done, but we also have to remember he has been playing through injury and behind an offensive line that has been putrid. The Raiders rank dead last in yards before contact per attempt (0.97). The Packers are 31st, and they have generated 1.28 yards before contact per attempt just for context. Jeanty has a wide range of outcomes this week, but even if his previous role comes back, he has a tough matchup. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Saquon Barkley played only 32.4% of the snaps with a 44.8% rushing share and a 16.3% route share (2.9% target share). Last week, Barkley finished with 14 touches and 54 total yards (one touchdown). Barkley was the RB22 in weekly scoring. In the last two weeks, Barkley has had an 11.8% explosive run rate, 2.55 yards after contact per attempt, and a 20% missed tackle rate. These are all amazing numbers considering Barkley has been playing with one healthy leg and a balky back. Barkley can get it done this week on limited volume. Over the last five games, New York has allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 15th-most yards after contact per attempt. Barkley opened the week with a DNP.

Last week, Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight got injured, and Tyler Allgeier became the team's bell-cow runner against Dallas. Allgeier responded with 16 touches and 191 total yards (two scores) as the RB1 for the week. I don't expect that type of output from Allgeier moving forward, especially this week, but he will be a volume-fueled running back option for lineups. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allgeier is first in yards after contact per attempt and 31st in missed tackle rate. This week, he'll need all the volume he can handle and a touchdown to pay off for fantasy. Seattle has shut down rushers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the 11th-lowest rushing success rate, and the eighth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Devin Singletary should operate as the Giants' workhorse this week, with only Singletary and Greg Desrosiers healthy in the running back room. This season, in limited duty, Singletary has posted a solid 2.11 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. He should flirt with 15-18 touches this week with a nice matchup incoming. Singletary is an RB2 this week. Over the last five games, Philly's run defense has been leaky, allowing the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the eighth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Rachaad White had to deal with Jeremy McNichols and Austin Ekeler cutting into his workload. With McNichols placed on IR, White will likely only have to deal with Ekeler this week, but Robert Henry Jr. could get into the mix, and I wouldn't be shocked. Last week, White played 47.4% of the snaps with 42.3% of the rushing work and a 39.4% route share (10.3% target share). White finished with 12 touches and 60 total yards (one score) as the RB15 for the week. White has posted a solid 17% missed tackle rate this season but a disappointing 1.87 yards after contact per attempt. White will need to make the most of his volume and likely get into the endzone to pay off for fantasy this week. The matchup is rough. The Rams' run defense has improved. Over the last five games, they have allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate, the 11th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fourth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Breece Hall will be back this week. With that said, I don't know what to do with the Jets backfield. I can envision an easy scenario where Hall is immediately reinstalled as the Jets' workhorse this week, but I can also understand if New York wants to deploy a committee or have a hot hand approach this week. Braelon Allen was absolutely awesome with Hall out, so it's likely tough to put that tackle-breaking genie back in the bottle. Among 42 qualifying backs, Hall is 20th in explosive run rate, 41st in yards after contact per attempt, and 27th in missed tackle rate. Hall hasn't been immensely efficient with his workload this season even before dealing with the injury. With workload questions this week, Hall needs to be as efficient as possible with his touches, but that will be tough against the Chiefs' stout run defense. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. Hall could be a volume-based RB2 this week or a touchdown-needy RB3/flex.

Since Week 5, Alvin Kamara has had a 36.9% snap rate, 22.2% of the rushing work, and a 32.3% route share (14% target share). Since Week 5, he has averaged nine touches and 45.7 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 12.5% explosive run rate, 2.19 yards after contact per attempt, and a 31% missed tackle rate. Those numbers imply Kamara is getting healthier because he hasn't posted numbers like that until this point in the season. Kamara could surprise with a strong showing this week. The Browns have been bleeding out production to backs. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the second-highest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate. With Kendre Miller released, I expect Kamara's role to grow this week.

Last week, Jadarian Price surprisingly led the backfield with a 48.2% snap rate, a 52.6% rushing share, and a 33.3% route share. Price finished with 12 touches and 37 total yards. The red zone work was split up between Price and Zach Charbonnet, with Price seeing one carry inside the 20-yard line while Charbonnet had two. Price has been efficient with his workload this season with 2.55 yards after contact per attempt and a 24% missed tackle rate. I have no clue if he'll continue to lead the way for Seattle's ground game, though. That was Zach Charbonnet's first game back in the lineup, and I expect his role to grow moving forward. Price will need volume this week and a score to pay off as a flex this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Blake Corum is on fire! Since Week 5, he has been the RB13 in fantasy points per game, averaging 12 touches and 76.6 total yards. Corum has scored a touchdown in each of his last four games. Among 42 qualifying backs, Corum is seventh in explosive run rate and 17th in missed tackle rate. This could be the week that Corum's hot streak ends, though. Over their last five games, Washington has tightened up the run defense, allowing the fifth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Braelon Allen could immediately return to operating as Breece Hall's understudy, or he could force a committee. Allen was fantastic with Hall out. In Weeks 4-8, Allen averaged 21.2 touches and 114.8 total yards as the RB15 in fantasy points per game. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allen is third in explosive run rate, seventh in yards after contact per attempt, and 14th in missed tackle rate. If the Jets open Week 9 with a hot hand approach with their backfield, don't be surprised if Allen has the warmer mitts. Allen's range of outcomes is wide. He could be a decent RB2 or a touchdown-needy flex this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week was Zach Charbonnet's first game back. Charbonnet finished with nine touches and 29 total yards while leading the backfield with two red zone rushing attempts. Charbonnet was second on the team in backfield snap rate (35.7%), rushing share (31.6%), and route share (17.9%). He has only 1.67 yards after contact per attempt but a solid 17% missed tackle rate. Charbonnet's workload is likely to grow moving forward, but I don't want to flex him this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Over the last two games, Jordan Mason has been the Vikings' lead back, averaging only 12.5 touches and 44 total yards. Mason has had a 46.2% snap rate, 48.9% of the rushing work, and a 24.2% route share. He has led the Minny backfield in each of those categories over the last two games. Mason has posted a disappointing 1.89 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate this season. With the limited volume and effectiveness, Mason is a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two weeks, Aaron Jones has been a committee back with Jordan Mason, averaging eight touches and 33 total yards. In those games, he has had a 32.1% snap rate, 27.7% of the rushing attempts, and a 21% route share. Mason has bested him in each of those categories as Minny's lead back. Jones has shown his age this season with only 1.97 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate. He's a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Dylan Sampson has had a 50.1% snap rate, a 15.9% rushing share, a 47.7% route share, and an 11.7% target share. Sampson has averaged eight touches and 73 total yards. In those two games, Sampson has had a 21% TPRR with an eye-popping 2.24 YPRR and a red zone target. With his minuscule rushing work, he has also had 2.43 yards after contact per attempt and a 14.3 explosive run rate. Sampson is a strong flex play this week, especially in PPR formats. He has been the RB28 and RB19 over the last two weeks. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the third-highest yards per target, the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the tenth-most receiving yards to running backs. Sampson should also be able to make the most of his carries this week. Over their last five games, the Saints have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-highest missed tackle rate.

The Bucs have leaned extremely run-heavy over the last two games. In that span, Kenneth Gainwell has averaged 19.5 carries and 114 rushing yards as the RB35 in fantasy points per game. Gainwell has been awesome on a per-touch basis this season with a 15.5% explosive run rate, 3.09 yards after contact per attempt, and a 29% missed tackle rate. We'll see if the Bucs continue this run-centric offense in Week 9 or if the Bears can pry them away from it, but Gainwell is still a solid flex this week. Last week, the Bears' run defense looked like a force, with Jeffery Simmons clogging up the middle. They allowed only a 26.3% rushing success rate, -0.57 rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and 1.68 yards after contact per attempt. Gainwell won't have an easy road this week, but if he gets 10-15 touches, he can still be flex-worthy.

Last week was just more of the same for Omarion Hampton. He finished with 11 touches and 27 total yards. He had only a 30.5% snap rate, 36% of the rushing work, and an 18.9% route share. If any player not named Omarion Hampton had this lengthy resume of underperformance entering Week 9, he'd be dropped in every league. Hampton has a decent 2.33 yards after contact per attempt, but his 8.6% explosive run rate and 13% missed tackle rate are eye sores. This is another week to sit Hampton. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 14th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Mike Washington took over as the team's lead back last week, but I don't know how long that will last. The workload could easily bounce back in the direction of Ashton Jeanty this week if this were all related to his quotes about the Jets' run defense. I have no clue if it's related, but we'll find out how this all shakes out this week. In Weeks 1-7, Washington had a 20.9% snap rate, averaging 6.1 touches and 29.5 total yards. Last week, he played 63.3% of the snaps with 75.8% of the rushing work, and an 18.5% route share. Washington finished with 25 carries and 83 rushing yards. Washington has to run behind the same horrible offensive line that Jeanty does. Washington has managed a 12.3% explosive run rates nd 2.37 yards after contact per attempt, though. Washington's usage and volume are up in the air this week, but he has a horrible matchup incoming and is best left on the bench. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

With Bhayshul Tuten active, Chris Rodriguez could still see an elevated role this week. Rodriguez has had a 24.3% snap rate while averaging 6.7 touches and 33.2 total yards. Among 45 qualifying rushers, Rodriguez is 20th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Rodriguez is a touchdown-dependent flex. Baltimore hasn't been an easy team to run on. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, but there is a sliver of hope here. Over the same time span, this run defense has also had the fourth-lowest rate of hitting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage, and it has allowed the 11th-highest gap rushing success rate (Rodriguez 53.3% gap).

Christian McCaffrey's hamstring isn't 100%. With McCaffrey operating at less than full health and a nice rushing matchup incoming, I wouldn't be surprised to see Kaelon Black see 12-15 carries against the Raiders. Black has seen at least 12 carries in two games this season while averaging 8.5 touches and 33.9 total yards per game. Black hasn't been impressive as a rusher with only a 7% explosive run rate and 7% missed tackle rate, but that might not matter this week. The Raiders' run defense has been that bad. Over their last five games, Las Vegas has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the most yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, with Jonah Coleman leading the way, J.K. Dobbins has seen his role reduced. In those games, Dobbins has had a 22% offensive snap rate with 6.5 rushing attempts and 18 rushing yards per game. Dobbins is a low-end, touchdown-dependent flex until that changes. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Kyle Monangai could be back this week. Monangai didn't practice until Friday this week (thumb/toe). He has been listed as questionable. Monangai is the RB16 in fantasy points per game this season, averaging 16.3 touches and 90.8 total yards. Among 42 qualifying rushers, Monangai is ninth in explosive run rate, second in yards after contact per attempt, and sixth in missed tackle rate. I don't expect Chicago to load him up with volume this week, but he could still be a solid flex this week. Over their last five games, Tampa Bay has allowed the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, the eighth-highest zone yards per carry, and the 13th-highest zone rushing success rate (Monangai: 70% zone).

Cam Skattebo didn't practice until Friday of this week (hamstring). He only managed a limited session on Friday and has been listed as doubtful. I expect Skattebo to miss this week, which means Devin Singletary should operate as the Giants' workhorse this week.
